channel.title: Emory Financial Insights
channel.description: Plain-English articles from California mortgage broker Derek Shao on homeownership, home equity, family property and the economy, and what each means for your mortgage.

item.title: Stocks Just Had Their Worst Week Since April 2025. Is Your Down Payment in the Market? What California Buyers Should Know
item.description: Stocks fell about 8.6% last week as bond yields dropped. How lenders count stocks, funds and 401(k)s for a down payment, and when to move money to cash.

item.title: Buying a Home Soon? Read This Before You Open a Store Card or Use Buy Now, Pay Later This Black Friday
item.description: A new store card, BNPL plan or financed TV can change your mortgage approval. How lenders check for new debt before closing, and what to do instead.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Jumped Back Above 7.25%. Is Paying Points to Lower Your Rate Worth It Right Now?
item.description: Rates rose to a 7.28% national average this week. How discount points work, how to find your break-even, the tax rules and when points backfire.

item.title: Putting Your California Home in a Living Trust? What Happens to Your Mortgage, Your Property Taxes and Your Next Refinance
item.description: Moving your California home into a living trust won't trigger your mortgage's due-on-sale clause or a reassessment if done right. Here's what to know.

item.title: California Home Sales Fell to a Nearly Three-Year Low in October. Prices Barely Moved. What That Means for Buyers and Sellers This Winter
item.description: California home sales fell 12.7% in October 2026 while the median price held near $887,000. What it means for buyers and sellers this winter.

item.title: Builders Are Cutting Prices and Buying Down Rates. Should California Buyers Take a Fresh Look at New Construction?
item.description: Builder confidence hit its lowest since 2012 and 68% of builders offer incentives. How builder rate buydowns work and what California buyers should check.

item.title: A Historic El Niño Is Building, and Your Homeowners Policy Doesn't Cover Floods. What California Owners and Buyers Should Do Before December
item.description: Most California home policies exclude flooding, and federal flood coverage usually takes 30 days to start. What to do before El Niño storms arrive.

item.title: Rates Are Climbing Again. Can You Take Over a Seller's Low-Rate Mortgage? Assumable FHA and VA Loans in California
item.description: With rates back above 7%, some buyers can assume a seller's FHA or VA loan. Who qualifies, the equity gap, fees, timelines and what VA sellers risk.

item.title: Buying a Truck or Equipment Before December 31? What That Write-Off Means for Your 2027 Mortgage
item.description: Self-employed and buying in 2027? How lenders treat a year-end truck or equipment write-off, the cash you spend, and any new loan payment.

item.title: Still Paying Mortgage Insurance? How California Homeowners Can Drop PMI Without Refinancing
item.description: Fannie Mae now lets servicers tell you when you may qualify to cancel PMI. The 80%, 78% and 75% rules, appraisal steps, and what FHA borrowers can do.

item.title: Closing on a Home in December? The Holiday Dates, Property Tax Bills and Tax Rules California Buyers Should Know
item.description: Thanksgiving and Christmas shift closing deadlines, the Dec 10 tax installment is due, and Dec 31 decides which tax year counts. A guide for CA buyers.

item.title: Inflation Came In Hot, and a Fed Governor Put a Half-Point Hike on the Table. What It Means for Your HELOC and Mortgage
item.description: October prices rose 0.4%, above forecasts, and Fed Governor Waller said a half-point December hike should be considered. What it means for HELOCs, locks.

item.title: Your Mortgage Credit Score Is Changing: VantageScore, FICO and What California Buyers Should Do Before 2027
item.description: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac now accept VantageScore 4.0 from all lenders, and FHA follows January 1. What it means for your score and your loan.

item.title: Veterans Day: How a VA Home Loan Works in California's High-Cost Market, and the Property Tax Break Many Disabled Veterans Miss
item.description: VA loans can mean no down payment and no mortgage insurance at California prices. How entitlement, funding fees and the veterans tax exemption work.

item.title: Mortgage Delinquencies Are Ticking Up. Behind on Your Payment in California? Your Options and Your Rights
item.description: Late payments rose again in FHFA's latest report. If you're behind in California, here are your options, your rights and the foreclosure timeline.

item.title: The IRS Just Raised the Gift Limit to $20,000 for 2027. Helping a Child With a Down Payment? Here's How Timing Works
item.description: The IRS set the 2027 annual gift exclusion at $20,000, up from $19,000. How December and January gifts work for a California down payment.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Fell Three Weeks Straight. Then Today's Jobs Report Came In Hot. Lock or Float?
item.description: Freddie Mac's 30-year average fell to 7.18%, then a strong October jobs report lifted yields. What California buyers in escrow should know about locks.

item.title: Changing Jobs Before You Buy? How Lenders Treat a New Job, an Offer Letter or a January Start Date
item.description: A new job doesn't have to stop a California home purchase. How lenders treat salary, hourly pay, offer letters and gaps, and what to do before you switch.

item.title: Voters Approved Prop 37 and Prop 1 Is Projected to Pass. What California Homebuyers Should Know Now
item.description: Prop 37 passed and Prop 1 is projected to pass. What happens next, when help could arrive, and what California buyers should do in the meantime.

item.title: Only 19% of Californians Can Afford a Median-Priced Home. Here's the Income It Takes in Your County
item.description: C.A.R. says 19% of California households could afford a median-priced home in Q3 2026. The income needed by county, and ways buyers are closing the gap.

item.title: Counting on Your Bonus, Commission or Overtime to Buy in 2027? How Lenders Actually Count It
item.description: Planning to buy in 2027 on bonus, commission or overtime pay? How lenders average it, why a dip hurts, and what to do before year-end.

item.title: Should You Pay Your Second Property Tax Installment Before December 31? The 2026 SALT Cap, Explained for California Homeowners
item.description: The SALT cap is $40,400 for 2026. When paying your spring property tax installment in December helps, when it doesn't, and what to tell your servicer.

item.title: Got an Escrow Shortage Letter? Why California Mortgage Payments Are Rising This Fall and What You Can Do
item.description: Rising insurance and new tax bills are triggering escrow shortages. What the letter means, your rights under federal rules, and how to lower the hit.

item.title: Some Lenders Are Already Using 2027 Loan Limits. What California Buyers Near the Jumbo Line Should Know
item.description: FHFA sets 2027 conforming loan limits in late November. Here's where California counties stand, why some lenders moved early, and what it means for you.

item.title: LA Fire Survivors: Lenders' Insurance-Payout Reports Are Due Today. Here's What Your Mortgage Company Owes You
item.description: California ordered lenders to report by Oct. 29 on LA fire insurance payouts. What your servicer owes you, including 2% interest under AB 493.

item.title: The Fed Held Rates Today. Two Officials Wanted a Hike. Here's What It Means for Your HELOC and Mortgage
item.description: The Fed held rates at 3.75%–4% on October 28, with two officials voting to hike. What it means for California HELOCs, ARMs, fixed loans and rate locks.

item.title: Your 2026–27 Property Tax Bill Is Arriving: What LA County Homeowners Should Check Before December 10
item.description: LA County's 2026–27 tax bills are due Nov. 1 and late after Dec. 10. What to check: escrow, supplemental bills, the homeowners' exemption and appeals.

item.title: California Home Insurance This Fall: What Buyers and Homeowners Should Know Before They Renew or Make an Offer
item.description: New CDI rate-review transparency, slowing FAIR Plan growth and what lenders require: how California home insurance affects buyers and owners now.

item.title: The Fed Meets This Week: What a Hold or Another Hike Means for Your HELOC, Mortgage and Rate Lock
item.description: The Fed decides on rates October 28 after September's hike. What it means for California HELOCs, adjustable loans, fixed mortgages and rate locks.

item.title: Two Backyard ADUs on One Lot: What California's New ADU Laws Mean for Homeowners in 2027
item.description: From Jan. 1, 2027, California cities must approve two detached ADUs per single-family lot. What AB 956 and SB 1117 change, and the financing catch.

item.title: Prop 1 on Your November 3 Ballot: What California's $11.25 Billion Housing Bond Means for Buyers, Renters and Veterans
item.description: Prop 1 would borrow $11.25 billion for housing, including $1.1 billion for first-time buyers. Where it goes, what it costs, and what each side says.

item.title: California Home Sales Slowed in September. Here's How Buyers Can Use Seller Credits Right Now
item.description: California home sales fell 6.5% in September 2026 while prices held. How seller credits and rate buydowns work, and the Fannie Mae and FHA limits.

item.title: California's New HOA Reserve Law (AB 2050): What Condo Owners and Buyers Need to Know
item.description: AB 2050, signed Sept. 29, 2026, requires some California HOAs to put 15% of their budget into reserves from 2032. What it means for dues and condo loans.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Climbed Past 7.4% This Fall: What California Homeowners and Buyers Should Do Now
item.description: Freddie Mac's 30-year average hit 7.40% in October 2026 after a fall climb. What it means for California refis, HELOCs, rate locks and buyers.

item.title: Prop 37 on California's November Ballot: A State Down Payment Loan for New Homes, Explained
item.description: Prop 37 would let CalHFA lend middle-income buyers up to 17% of a new home's price. How it would work, who qualifies, and what each side says.

item.title: The FAIR Plan's 29% Rate Increase Is Here: What It Means for Your Mortgage Payment
item.description: California FAIR Plan rates rose an average 29.1% on Oct. 15, 2026. How it hits your escrow, what lenders require, and steps to lower your premium.

item.title: LA's Prop TE on the November Ballot: What It Means for Palisades Fire Homeowners Who Sell
item.description: Prop TE would exempt Palisades Fire-damaged homes sold by 2030 from LA's Measure ULA mansion tax. What it does, who qualifies, and both sides, explained.

item.title: Helping Your Adult Child Buy a Home: Gift, Co-Sign, or Co-Borrow?
item.description: Want to help your son or daughter buy in California? Compare a gift, co-signing and co-borrowing, with 2026 gift tax limits and what lenders require.

item.title: Divorce and the Family Home in California: Keep It, Sell It, or Buy Out Your Spouse?
item.description: Going through a divorce in California? How community property, spousal buyouts, Prop 13 and capital gains work, and how to refinance your ex off the loan.

item.title: Building an ADU in California: For Family or Rental Income, and How to Pay for It
item.description: An ADU for your parents, adult kids or rental income? California's 2026 ADU rules, how lenders count ADU rent, and the ways to finance one.

item.title: HELOC vs. Cash-Out Refinance: How to Tap Your Equity Without Giving Up a Low Rate
item.description: Half of U.S. homeowners have a mortgage rate under 4%. Here's when a HELOC beats a cash-out refinance, when it doesn't, and what the 2026 tax rules say.

item.title: Self-Employed and Planning to Buy? Start With Next Year's Tax Return
item.description: Write-offs that save you tax can shrink your mortgage. How lenders read self-employed returns, which deductions they add back, and a 12-month plan.

item.title: Worried About AI and Your Job? Here's What It Means for Your Mortgage
item.description: Worried AI could affect your job? A 20-year California mortgage broker explains what to do now to protect your home, your loan options, and your plans.

item.title: Earned Wage Access and Buying a Home: What Tradespeople and Gig Workers Should Know
item.description: Electricians, landscapers, pool techs and gig workers use pay-early apps. How earned wage access shows up when you apply for a California mortgage.

item.title: Buy, Remodel, or Tear Down and Rebuild? A California Homeowner's Decision Guide
item.description: Outgrowing your home? Compare buying, remodeling and rebuilding in California: property tax, financing options and a checklist to pick your path.

item.title: Inheriting Your Parents' California Home: Prop 19, Property Taxes, and Sibling Buyouts
item.description: Plan to keep your parents' California home? How Prop 19's $1,044,586 exclusion works, what it means for property tax, and how to finance a sibling buyout.

item.title: Should You Pay Off Your Mortgage Early or Invest the Difference?
item.description: Extra mortgage payments vs. investing: a California mortgage broker runs the numbers for 3% and 6.75% loans and shows how to decide what fits your family.
